scenes.narration: Wild coffee plants grew in the forests of Ethiopia long before anyone brewed a cup. By the fifteenth century, Sufi monks in Yemen were drinking it to stay awake through night prayers.
From Yemen it spread to Mecca, Cairo, Damascus and Istanbul. Coffee houses became the places where people met, argued and shared news.
In 1720, Gabriel de Clieu carried coffee seedlings to Martinique. Within decades the Caribbean was supplying much of the world's coffee.
By 1852 Brazil was the largest producer on Earth, and it still is. Every cup today traces back to those Ethiopian forests.

youtube.title: How Coffee Conquered the World
youtube.description: From Ethiopian forests to Brazil's plantations: the short history of coffee.
